titleStmt.title: Efficient Response Time Bound for Typed DAG Tasks

analytic.title: Efficient Response Time Bound for Typed DAG Tasks

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Heterogeneous multi-core platforms have been used in many fields to meet the increasing requirement of computation. In this paper, we study the response time bound of typed DAG (directed acyclic graph) tasks on heterogeneous multi-core platforms. The existing bound has exponential time complexity. In this paper, we propose a new bound that can be computed with complexity O(|V |+|E|) and is only slightly larger than the stateof-the-art. Experiments demonstrate that the computation of our bound is significantly more efficient than the existing bound and our bound has almost the same tightness as the existing bound. Index Terms-response time bound, typed DAG task, heterogeneous multi-core 226 2023 IEEE 29th International Conference on Embedded and Real-Time Computing Systems and Applications (RTCSA)

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: In the last decade, multi-core platform has attracted growing attention due to increasing high-performance and realtime requirements. On one hand, heterogeneous multi-core platforms, which integrate different types of processors on a single chip, allow it to realize a more fine-grained execution arrangement and thus generally lead to higher performance [1] and lower energy consumption [2]. Now, multi-cores with heterogeneous architecture are deployed in many fields, such as image processing, machine learning, autonomous driving, etc. For example, ARM processors and GPUs are integrated into Samsung Exynos [3] and NVIDIA Tegra [4] SoCs. On the other hand, for these applications to be deployed in real-time systems with heterogeneous platforms, the timing behaviors should be theoretically guaranteed in advance. Therefore, practical and efficient analysis techniques for real-time applications on heterogeneous platforms are of critical importance.

The typed DAG (Directed acyclic graph) task model, where each vertex is explicitly bound to a particular type of cores, can be used to model the behaviors of real-time applications on heterogeneous platforms. Response time analysis of typed DAG tasks has gradually been noticed by researchers in realtime community. Previous result on typed DAG tasks [5] is too pessimistic and suffers from non-self-sustainability (i.e., the response time bound can be larger if provided with more cores). Recently, Han et al. [6] proposed a response time bound that is much tighter than [5] and solves the non-selfsustainability issue. Unfortunately, computing Han's bound is strongly NP-hard [6]. If the typed DAG task and the underline heterogeneous platform become complex, the time required to compute Han's bound increases rapidly, which renders Han's bound impractical for the analysis of realistic applications.

In this paper, we propose a new response time bound for typed DAG tasks on heterogeneous platforms. On one hand, our bound has polynomial time complexity O(|V | + |E|) and thus can be computed quite efficiently. On the other hand, our bound is only slightly larger than Han's bound. Actually, evaluation shows that for most cases, our bound is the same as Han's bound. To achieve this, first, we present an algorithm to adjust the interference set of vertices in typed DAG tasks while keeping the resulting response time bound safe at the same time (Section III). Second, we prove that under the adjusted interference set, the algorithm in [7] can be employed to compute the response time bound (Section IV). Experimental evaluations demonstrate that compared to Han's bound, our method can significantly reduce the computing time of the proposed bound and keep the bound tight as Han's bound.

div.head: A. Task Model
div.p: We consider typed tasks to execute on a multi-core platform with different types of cores. We denote the set of types by S. Each s ∈ S represents a type with M s identical cores. A typed task is modeled as a DAG G = (V, E), where V = {v 1 , • • • , v n } is the set of vertices, and E ⊆ V × V represents the set of directed edges. In the typed model, every vertex is characterized by a worst-case execution time (WCET) c(v i ) and a type t(v i ). A vertex v i can execute at most c(v i ) time units on the cores of type t(v i ).
An edge (u, v) ∈ E shows the precedence relationship between u and v. We say u is a predecessor of v and v is a
div.formula: successor of u, if v can only start to execute after u finishes. A path of G is denoted by λ = {v 0 , • • • , v k }, where ∀i ∈ [0, k), (v i , v i+1 ) ∈ E, and we define len(λ) = k i=0 c(v i ) as the length of λ. If a path (v 0 , • • • , v k ) satisfies v 0 = v src and v k = v snk ,
div.p: we call this path a complete path. We use len(G) to denote the length of the longest path of G. If there exists a path from u to v, we call u an ancestor of v and v a descendant of u. We use pred(v), succ(v), ance(v), and desc(v) to denote the set of predecessors, successors, ancestors, and descendants of v, respectively.

We call a vertex with no predecessor as a source (denote as v src ) and with no successor as a sink (denote as v snk ). Without loss of generality, we assume that a DAG has exactly one source and one sink. If a DAG has multiple sources (multiple sinks), a dummy source (sink) with 0 WCET and a random type is added to this DAG with edges to (from) all the sources (sinks) of the original DAG. For any vertices set V ⊆ V , we define vol(V ) = v∈V c(v) as the total WCET of vertices in V . And vol(G) denotes the total WCET of a DAG G. Example 1. Fig. 1 shows a DAG task with 7 vertices. div.p: Execution Sequence. At runtime, a scheduling algorithm decides which vertex to execute at a specific time on a specific core. We call such a trace description an execution sequence. The execution time of a vertex v may be less than c(v) and a scheduling algorithm may have non-determinism, which may result in different execution sequences generated by the same scheduling algorithm with the same G. To analyze the runtime behavior, we use f (v) to denote the time point when v finishes. Example 2. Fig. 2 illustrates an execution sequence of Fig. 1. Work-conserving scheduling means an eligible vertex must be executed if there are available cores with the same type of the vertex. div.head: V. EVALUATION
div.p: In this section, we evaluate the performance of our proposed response time bound in terms of efficiency and tightness. We first define a default parameters range and tune only one parameter once to show how it influences the performance of our bound. The detailed settings of our evaluation are defined as follows:

• 1000 DAG tasks for every experiment setting. • To ensure that the utilization of every type is not larger than its core number, we assign the total WCET of every s ∈ S by vol(G)×Ms t∈S Mt . • We assign the total WCET of every type to the vertices through the UUnifast [8] method. We run experiments on Ubuntu 18.04 with an Intel i7-10700 CPU (8 cores 16 threads and 4.6 GHz) and 16GB RAM. We compare our bound (the NEW-TYPED in the figure) to the bounds in [6] (HAN-NEWB1 and HAN-NEWB2) and the bound in [5] (OLD-B). Fig. 4 reports the normalized WCRT bounds regarding OLD-B. All figures in Fig. 4 show that our bound is close to HAN-NEWB2 and both are more precise than OLD-B and HAN-NEWB1. This is because our adjusted interference set is similar, even equal to the interference set of HAN-NEWB2 in most cases.

Fig. 4c suggests that HAN-NEWB1 is closer to NEW-TYPED and HAN-NEWB2 when pr is increasing. The reason is that larger pr means a more sequential task, and the proportion of vertices in the critical path is bigger, which causes that HAN-NEWB1 is closer to NEW-TYPED and HAN-NEWB2's. When the task is completely sequential (pr = 1), all vertices are in the critical path, so HAN-NEWB1 is equal to NEW-TYPED and HAN-NEWB2 when pr = 1.

In Fig. 4d, the result shows that when there are more types, NEW-TYPED and HAN-NEWB2 are more precise than HAN-NEWB1 because HAN-NEWB1 just considers the type with the largest M s . When the number of types is 1, NEW-TYPED and HAN-NEWB2 will degrade to HAN-NEWB1. Average execution time (ms) Fig. 5 shows the execution time under different parameter settings. Our NEW-TYPED is much more efficient than HAN-NEWB2. Furthermore, Fig. 5(b,c,d) shows that when |V |, |S| increases or pr decreases, the efficiency of HAN-NEWB2 suffers quickly, but the execution time of NEW-TYPED increases slowly or almost stays constant, which means that the computing efficiency of our NEW-TYPED is significantly better than HAN-NEWB2.

div.head: VI. RELATED WORK
div.p: For the analysis of a single typed DAG task on heterogeneous multi-core platforms, [5] proposed a response time bound that is too pessimistic and suffers from non-selfsustainability (i.e., the response time bound can be larger if provided with more computing resources). In [6], Han et al. proposed two response time bounds. The first bound has the same time complexity as the bound in [5] but is still two pessimistic which can result in a large portion of computing resources being wasted when deployed in practice. The second bound is much smaller than the first bound. However, the second bound is strongly NP-hard. Computing the second bound for realistic applications with many different types of cores and many subtasks is infeasible. Chang et al. [9] proposed an approach that assigns criticality to vertices in the typed DAG task, thus improving the response time bound. The scheduling algorithm of [9] is different from the one studied in this paper. [10] studied the exact WCRT for typed DAG tasks on heterogeneous multi-core processors. The method of [10] is also strongly NP-hard, and only of theoretical value.

For the scheduling of multiple typed DAG tasks, [11] proposed a federated scheduling approach for typed DAG tasks. [12] proposed type-aware federated scheduling algorithms for sporadic typed DAG tasks with implicit deadlines running on a heterogeneous platform with two different types of cores. [13] studied the global fixed-priority scheduling of typed DAG tasks.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we propose a response time bound for a typed DAG task executing on heterogeneous multi-core platforms. Experiments show that our bound has an extremely similar tightness to the state-of-the-art (HAN-NEWB2) and has high computing efficiency. In the future, we would like to find out how to reduce the difference between our adjusted interference set and the interference set of HAN-NEWB2.
